title: Gods Made by the Carpenter
english: … and let these too be cast down behind the glory of God. And if all the nations, he says, are as nothing and have been counted as nothing, “with what likeness have you likened Him?” (Isaiah 40:17-18). For what will be like Him and of equal weight with Him, whether in nature, or in weight, or even in the measure of glory? Is it by the arts of a carpenter and the skill of a woodworker? Is it by goldsmiths? Or has He been shaped, as in an image, to resemble any creature at all? That is, he says, has a statue in the form of a man been made? Not at all. For nothing could be equal to Him. Since He is God by nature, and there is no other beside Him, He will surely be above all things in every way.

Having shown, then, that He is beyond everything that has been made and called into being, he next laughs to scorn the making of idols, and says: “The carpenter chooses wood that does not rot, and wisely seeks how he will set up his image so that it may not totter” (Isaiah 40:20). So it would be the work of the carpenter's skill, by the measure of the intelligence he has, to construct a god for those in error as they see fit, and to secure it with the greatest care so that it may not totter and fall and be shattered. So the worshippers of idols would be short of gods if there were no carpenter's skill on earth! Nor would the handmade things, once made, have been kept safe, unless the craftsman had wisely sought the means by which they could stand and keep an unshaken seat.

One might say, I think, and very fittingly, what was spoken through the voice of David: “The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the works of men's hands” (Psalm 135:15). And to this he adds: “May all who make them become like them, and all who trust in them” (Psalm 135:18).

Having laughed to scorn, then, the fashioning of idols, he turns his discourse to shame and correct those who have gone astray, and shows that their offence in this is without excuse, saying: “Will you not know? Will you not hear?” (Isaiah 40:21), instead of “Did you not know? Did you not hear?” “Has it not been told to you from the beginning? Have you not known the foundations of the earth?” By the foundations of the earth he means its farthest parts and its ends. So you have known, he says, you who live from one end of it to the other. You have heard, and it has been told to you from the beginning.

And what has been told? That God, who is God by nature and in truth, is one and alone; but the things men craft into gods for us are wood and stones and nothing else. For the God-inspired Scripture has not kept silent; rather, the knowledge of the truth has been proclaimed from of old, through patriarchs, through the Law and the Prophets. For it was not when the only-begotten Word of God, having become like us, shone forth as man on those upon the earth, that they first fell under the gravest charge of going astray. No, as I said, the charge of idolatry was ancient. For He did not cease …

title: Righteousness Raised from the East
english: All will say the same thing to those being taught the mysteries. For since they speak from one Spirit, they will not fight against each other's words; rather, they will make their proclamation about the divine doctrines in harmony, and will announce, in a hidden way, the mystery of Christ. For this, I think, is the meaning of “Then let them declare judgment” (Isaiah 41:1). For since those of Israel called the Law given through Moses “judgment,” he very fittingly sets against it the saving proclamation of the Gospel, and by these words calls that “judgment.”

For true righteous judgment, and the force of a lawgiving that pleases God, does not shine out in the shadow of the Law, but rather in the proclamation of the holy teachers of the mysteries, the new rulers. They learned the judgment, that is, the will of God the Father, from Christ, and they have announced it to us as well, all saying the same thing.
“Who raised up righteousness from the east, and called it to follow at His heels, and it will go?” (Isaiah 41:2).

God, who holds authority over all things, should not be marvelled at only for the bare greatness of His works in creation; for He also gives proof of the gentleness that is in Him through the benefits He confers. For He has saved those upon the earth, and has rescued the human race, which had wholly perished, from death and corruption, and from the greed of the devil. For He has brought the devil to nothing, together with the powers that are with him, and He has justified us through faith, driving away the sin that had tyrannised over us.

But all these things were accomplished through Christ; for “He has become for us, from God the Father, righteousness and redemption and sanctification” (1 Corinthians 1:30). And we have been enlightened through Him, and have shared in mercy and love, and, in a word, in everything that has power to save. And this He foretold to us through one of the holy prophets, saying: “And for you who fear My name the sun of righteousness will rise, with healing in its wings” (Malachi 4:2).

Who, then, he says, caused righteousness to rise like the sun from the east, that is, Christ? Who called it, that is, caused it to come, and to appear in such a way that it walked at the heels of the One who called it, which is as much as to say that it followed in the very footsteps of God the Father? For so the Lord lived on earth, fulfilling the works of the Father and showing Him to us in His own nature. For He was and is equal to Him in power, and through the deeds themselves He has fully assured those on earth that He is in every respect equal in measure to the One who begot Him. Indeed, He said plainly: “If I do not do the works of My Father, do not believe Me. But if I do them, even though you do not believe Me, believe My works” (John 10:37-38). Following everywhere the will of the Father, or rather being itself …

title: Only God Knows What Is to Come
english: … God; “your counsels have drawn near,” says the King of Jacob (Isaiah 41:21).

He has declared very clearly how the calling of the nations will come about in its due time; He has promised to turn the desert into marshes and the thirsty land into watercourses, and to make it thick with cedars and box trees and other plants (Isaiah 41:18-19); and He has said that His own hand will be marvelled at as the Maker of such great things (Isaiah 41:20). Now He speaks again to the makers of idols and to the craftsmen of such things, and says that their judgment has come near. By judgment He means the punishment owed to them, that is, their shame and disgrace. For by the holy sentence of God and by a just judgment they would be punished, as men who have deceived the whole world under heaven and brought in counsels that are not true. For they taught those on earth to say to the wood, “You are my father,” and to the stone, “You begot me” (Jeremiah 2:27).

That is why He says that their counsels have drawn near, that is, have come to their end, since God is shaking down the error and scattering the mist of ignorance: not one of the gods they have, those falsely so called, we mean, but the Lord, God in truth, and the King of Jacob, that is, of those of the blood of Israel. By these words He brings to remembrance the signs that took place at the redemption of those of Israel, through which the power of the authority befitting God that is in Him, or of His incomparable pre-eminence, is very clearly recognised.

“Let them draw near and declare to you what will happen; or what the former things were, tell us, and we will set our mind on it, and we will know what the last things are and the things to come. Tell us, declare the things that are coming at the last, and we will know that you are gods. Do good, and do harm, and we will marvel and see together; for where are you from, and where is your work from? From the earth they chose you, an abomination” (Isaiah 41:22-24).

It is the proper and singular mark of the divine and ineffable glory to know all things and to be wholly ignorant of nothing, whether of what has happened before, or of what is present, or of what will be. Indeed, through the all-wise Moses He makes plain to those on earth the things before the framing of this world and the things at the beginning, saying: “In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth. And the earth was invisible and unformed, and darkness was over the abyss” (Genesis 1:1-2); and He goes through the making of the whole world most exactly.

But our Lord Jesus Christ too, who spoke those things of old through Moses, has declared to us the things at the end; for, as His disciple says, “We look for new heavens and a new earth, and His promises” (2 Peter 3:13). And one may hear Him saying plainly: “Will anything be hidden from Me?” (Jeremiah 32:27); and: “For the word of God is truly living, and clear, and …” (Hebrews 4:12).
